name: Cloudflare R2
summary: Cloudflare R2 is object storage for files like images and videos that never charges you for downloading data out of it.

free_plan_covers.note: Free tier includes 10 GB storage, 1 million write requests and 10 million read requests a month, plus unlimited free egress.

first_paid_usd_month.note: No monthly plan; R2 is pay-as-you-go at $0.015 per GB stored a month beyond the free 10 GB.

portability.note: R2 implements the S3 API, so existing S3 SDKs and tools work by pointing them at R2's endpoint URL.

direct_uploads.note: Browsers can upload directly to R2 using presigned URLs, generated with any S3-compatible SDK.

egress_fees.note: R2's main selling point: data transfer out to the internet is free on every plan, with no egress charge at all.

setup.step: Create a Cloudflare account, enable R2 in the dashboard, and create a bucket.
Create an R2 API token (Access Key ID and Secret Access Key) scoped to your bucket.
Install the AWS SDK for JavaScript with npm install @aws-sdk/client-s3 @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner, since R2 uses the S3-compatible API.
Configure the S3 client with region "auto" and your endpoint at https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com.
Generate presigned URLs on the server so the browser can upload directly to the bucket.

builder_notes: Use the S3-compatible SDK with region set to "auto" and the account-specific R2 endpoint, not an AWS region.
Generate presigned URLs on the server; never expose the R2 secret access key to the browser.
Because egress is free, R2 is a strong fit for apps that serve a lot of public downloads.
